analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata. Changes introduce paired update coordination, reversible admission drains and cluster candidate recovery, chiefly affecting A-018, TB-003, T-043 and the authorization-lifecycle contracts in T-053. No independently supported security regression was established in this scope.
LifecycleMailbox.swift:35-39 reuses existing atomic claims and private-file controls; head lines 54-61 and 88-96 enforce directory ownership, no-follow/nonblocking reads, regular-file checks and bounded input. ClusterUpdateDrain.swift:29-31 binds requests to process identity and bounds timestamps/timeouts. ClusterPairUpdate.swift:55-78 checks release agreement and working-phase freshness; lines 114-118 use a separate read/remove request path whose concurrency and filesystem guarantees depend on ClusterSupervisionFiles and its callers.
ClusterPairUpdateCycle.swift:1-474 stages through SelfUpdater verification, waits for local and peer drain status, correlates mailbox replies by request ID, and releases admission on unsuccessful exits. Integration must verify authenticated peer status via ClusterSetupLinkExchange, admission fencing while a part is starting or changes identity, and the reliability of the no-local-worker fallback before allowing an uncoordinated restart. These controls are outside this batch, not observed omissions.
ClusterCandidateRecovery.swift:45-79,114-162 uses update leases and persisted attempt state; lines 90-108 perform a timed version-output start check, not independent artifact qualification. Integration must inspect supervisor handling of lease/state failures, heartbeat-to-process/version binding, bounded child-process output/termination, and verified-predecessor rollback. T-043's same-binary recovery limitation must not be represented as resolved by this check.
No supplied change directly alters encryption, cache isolation (T-041), credential revocation, attestation policy or billing. Verify that reopening admission preserves current authorization checks rather than restoring stale permission. The indexed model's coverage of the new peer-controlled update/recovery interactions also needs reconciliation with the remaining PR evidence.
